data.coverage_note: NASA's reconstruction covers 8 separate stretches (30.1 hours in all); the numbers describe only those.

sunlight_h.no_margin_reason: Only the Moon's shadow is involved, cast by a smooth sphere: lunar mountains move its edges by seconds, which is not worked out here.

heard_h.no_margin_reason: Station masks are published without a tolerance.

longest_shadow_h.no_margin_reason: Only the Moon's shadow is involved, cast by a smooth sphere: lunar mountains move its edges by seconds, which is not worked out here.

longest_unheard_h.no_margin_reason: Its edges are set by station masks.

data.burns_note: No burn is found for this trip in the reconstruction, which covers 8 stretches, 30 h in all, between 2024-02-16 17:00 and 2024-02-21 05:00 UTC up to the arrival; any burn before it starts or in its gaps is not seen. Found where NASA's reconstruction leaves the force model by more than 0.05 m/s in half an hour, up to the arrival at the Moon; each is shown as one instant. A burn in a gap of the reconstruction is not seen. Burns in lunar orbit are not listed: there the force model and the reconstruction part by about 1 m/s at each close pass of the Moon, as much as a small burn.

corrections.label: A budget for these assumed errors, not a prediction of what the mission needed.

burns.name: First correction, a day after leaving Earth
Third correction, a day before arriving

linear_p99_m_s.no_margin_reason: The same errors pushed through the motion linearised about the plan.

assumptions.value: 0.5 m/s up or down, 1 m/s along the path, 0.5 m/s sideways

assumptions.what: Where the team thinks the lander is, at each correction

assumptions.value: 1 % of its size and 1 degree of pointing, plus 1 cm/s

corrections.plan_note: The flight as planned: NASA's reconstruction just before entering lunar orbit, propagated back to where it passed closest to Earth (622 km up, 170 min after the flown departure). Forward from there it arrives where and when the flown one did, with no burn on the way.
corrections.flown_note: No correction burn is seen in the reconstruction (any in its gaps are not seen).

belt_hours.missing_reason: NASA's reconstruction starts 242,208 km above Earth, beyond the belts, so the crossing of them is not in it and is not counted.

gcr_dose_mgy_day.source: From 18.9 cGy a year in silicon, measured by CRaTER's microdosimeter on LRO on 20 June 2009, about 10,000 km from the Moon (Mazur et al. 2011, as given by Schwadron et al. 2012, JGR 117, E00H13), scaled by the cosmic-ray model's change between then (W = 5) and 2024-02 (W = 91): ×0.40 (Matthiä et al. 2013, W from the Oulu neutron monitor, NMDB). ±30 % covers the scaling.

open_sky.no_margin_reason: From the site's skyline, the cosmic rays taken as arriving evenly from every direction; 1 is a flat horizon.

gcr_dose_mgy_day.source: From 13.2 ± 1 µGy an hour in silicon, measured on the surface by Chang'e-4's LND from January 2019 (Zhang et al. 2020, Science Advances 6, eaaz1334), its horizon taken as flat, scaled by the cosmic-ray model's change between then (W = 16) and 2024-02 (W = 91): ×0.44 (Matthiä et al. 2013, W from the Oulu neutron monitor, NMDB). ±30 % covers the scaling. Times the site's open sky (0.906).

radiation.sep_note: No solar particle event crossed NOAA's threshold (10 pfu above 10 MeV at GOES) during the trip (NASA DONKI).

fluence_gt10mev.no_margin_reason: As measured at 1 AU outside Earth's magnetic field (taken as arriving evenly from all directions); GOES proton detector, 5-minute averages (NOAA NCEI), 1989-10-19 12:00 to 1989-11-01 00:00 UTC; peak 42,200 pfu above 10 MeV (NOAA's list: 40,000).

As measured at 1 AU outside Earth's magnetic field (taken as arriving evenly from all directions); GOES proton detector, 5-minute averages (NOAA NCEI), 2003-10-28 11:00 to 2003-11-01 00:00 UTC; peak 29,500 pfu above 10 MeV (NOAA's list: 29,500).

As measured at 1 AU outside Earth's magnetic field (taken as arriving evenly from all directions); King (1974), J. Spacecraft Rockets 11, 401: fitted spectrum J(>E) = 7.9e9 exp((30 - E)/26.5) per cm², as SPENVIS gives it.

radiation.screening_note: Screening only: long-term average belt maps (good to about a factor of two), cosmic-ray dose scaled from measurements (±30 %), and past events as they were measured at 1 AU. None of it accounts for the spacecraft's own shielding. Confirm in SPENVIS, OLTARIS or CREME-MC before any design decision.

parts.note: A screening estimate: belt maps good to about a factor of two, cosmic-ray dose ±30 %; confirm in SPENVIS, OLTARIS or CREME-MC.
NASA's reconstruction as archived; its own accuracy is not published with it.
Spherical Earth and Moon; the ± on sunlight and the longest shadow is the change when Earth's shadow is made 2 % larger for its atmosphere.
A station 'can see' the spacecraft when it is above the station's mask; antenna pointing and bookings are not modelled.
